result:
Experiment 26's figure is written to `runs/20261102_125830_experiment26/figure.json`, and figcheck prints PASS.

I didn't draw a new figure. Experiment 26 re-runs experiment 21's design unchanged, because exp 21 never reached a GPU. So I copied exp 21's figure byte for byte: same graph and same changed stage, nothing to redraw. It shows the two EfficientNet-B0 trunks feeding the averaged belief map, the 3×3 pooled centroid and the min-confidence gate, all in ink. In the training band, the one thing in red is the new "epoch 0 = head-only probe" (probe first, then fine-tune), with the trunks held still.

I couldn't render the copied file myself: running Python to pull the SVG out of the JSON needed a permission that wasn't granted. Instead I looked at `fig.png`, the render of exp 21's figure saved in exp 21's folder. That picture is clean, with no overlaps or clipping and the input and output level on the centre line. Its footer ("…identical to exp 20") is still true for exp 26.

I left a three-line helper, `extract_svg.py`, in the exp 26 folder; it's harmless and you can delete it.
